chunks: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever intends a good deed, let him hasten to do it and not delay it, for sometimes the servant performs the deed, so Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, says: 'I have forgiven you and will not write anything against you ever.'

And whoever intends an evil deed, let him not do it, for sometimes the servant performs the evil, so Allah, Glorious is He, sees him and says: 'No, by My Honor and My Majesty, I will not forgive you after it ever.'

key_terms.هَمَّ: Intended or resolved in the heart

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between intending good and intending evil regarding divine forgiveness in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes the virtue of immediacy in worship, warning that delaying good deeds risks missing divine forgiveness, while committing evil invites a specific, irrevocable divine decree. This teaching highlights the Shia concept of *tawassul* through good deeds and the delicate balance between hope in mercy and fear of divine justice, urging believers to act on righteous intentions before they are forgotten or overridden by sin.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who intends a goodness, so let him hasten it and not delay it, for sometimes the servant performs the deed, so Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Blessed and High is Saying: “I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> have Forgiven (your sins) for you and will not Write anything against you, ever!”;

and the one who intends an evil, so he should not hasten it, for sometimes the servant would perform the evil, so Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, Glorious is He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, Sees him, and He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> is Saying: “No, by My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Honour and My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Majesty, I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> will not Forgive (your sins) for you after it, ever!”’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from certain individuals of our people from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Whoever intends to perform a good deed should act fast and do not delay. Perhaps a servant (of Allah) performs a deed and Allah, the Most Blessed, the Most High, says, ‘I have granted you forgiveness and will never write down anything against you.’

Whoever intends to perform an evil deed he must not do it. Perhaps a man does an evil deed and Allah, the Most Holy, sees it and says, “I swear by My Majesty and Glory to never forgive you hereafter.’”
